description.text: FTAI Aviation Ltd. (Nasdaq: FTAI) is a Cayman Islands exempted company. Except as otherwise specified, “we”, “us”, “our”, “FTAI”, “FTAI Aviation” or “the Company” refer to us and our consolidated subsidiaries. We are a leading independent engine maintenance platform focused on the CFM56-5B, CFM56-7B and V2500 aircraft engines which power the 737NG and A320ceo aircraft. We repair and rebuild engines in our maintenance facilities and with our joint venture partners, and sell or lease the engines to airlines and asset owners around the world. Our primary business model is to sell or lease engines via exchange through our proprietary Maintenance, Repair and Exchange (“MRE”) model which is reported under our Aerospace Products segment. We also own and manage a portfolio of on- and off-lease aircraft and engines through our Aviation Leasing segment. While historically these investment activities have been primarily held on balance sheet, at the end of 2024, we launched our Strategic Capital Initiative, which consists of an asset management business that manages third-party capital to invest in on-lease aircraft and engines. We expect our primary investment activities to be through our Strategic Capital Initiative going forward. As of December 31, 2025, we had total consolidated assets of $4.4 billion and total equity of $334.2 million.

analysis_md:
# FTAI — FTAI Aviation Ltd.

Pass-1 run, 2026-10-16, engine release 5.4.0. Price $169.29 (nasdaq_quote_api), market cap $17,580,244,071 — in scope under $40B. All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv, or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Aviation aftermarket and leasing platform built on the CFM56 and V2500 engine families (the engines on 737NG / A320ceo narrowbodies). Two segments: **Aerospace Products** — the proprietary Maintenance, Repair and Exchange (MRE) model: selling/exchanging refurbished engines and modules ("green time" optimization) instead of full shop visits; and **Aviation Leasing** — historically on-balance-sheet aircraft/engine leasing, now pivoting to the asset-light Strategic Capital Initiative (SCI): closed-end third-party vehicles (2025 SPV raised $2.0B equity, ~$6B deployed; 2026 SPV launched) that FTAI manages and co-invests in, with the SPV fleet captive to FTAI's MRE shops. New third leg: **FTAI Power** — run-out CFM56 cores converted to aeroderivative gas turbines for data-center power, anchored by a $1.465B customer contract for 2027 deliveries (Q2 2026 8-K). Q2 2026: revenue $953.1M (+40.9% YoY), net income $117.6M, Adjusted EBITDA $291.4M; dividend raised to $0.50/quarter.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow **−$310,745,000**; capex $27,712,000; SBC $21,733,000.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$360,190,000 = −$3.47/share** (base_oe_latest_per_share −3.4684709070892565).
- **Normalized base (3-yr median OE/share): −$2.00/share** (base_oe_per_share −2.001027488645108; the median year is FY2024, −$203,182,000 total).
- Maintenance version FY2025: −$338,457,000 — same ballpark, same sign.
- **OE positive in only 1 of the last 5 fiscal years** (oe_positive_years_of_last_5: 1/5 — FY2023, +$121,196,000 conservative). FY2021 −$179,376,000; FY2022 −$167,476,000; FY2024 −$203,182,000.
- Net debt $3,148,415,000 (TOTAL:LongTermDebt basis) against FY2025 book equity of $334,174,000 — debt/equity ~10x per the filed history (fundamentals.json debt-to-equity flagged at 10.3x for FY2025 in secondary coverage). This is a levered asset platform, not an asset-light compounder, on its own balance sheet.

**TTM check (ttm.py, through Q2 2026 — the STALE_FY resolution):** OCF FY −$310,745,000 − prior YTD −$136,284,000 + current YTD −$265,303,000 = **TTM OCF −$439,764,000**; capex TTM $40,643,000; SBC TTM $25,008,000; shares 104,039,259 → **TTM OE −$505,415,000 = −$4.86/share**. The TTM base is worse than both FY bases, so no --ttm run changes the verdict; the normalized median base stands and Tier F is not a staleness artifact.

**Why OCF is structurally negative here (the honest caveat):** FTAI's engine/module purchases for its exchange pool and resale flow through operating cash flow, while the proceeds and gains surface as revenue/gains — the model spends cash in OCF to build the asset pool it monetizes. That makes the conservative OE definition (OCF − capex − SBC) systematically harsh for this business in growth years. It does not rescue the score: even the maintenance definition and the latest FY are negative, net income's cash backing is the flagged problem below, and at $169.29 the market is capitalizing Adjusted EBITDA (~$1.25–1.3B guided for 2025, $2.3B segment guide for 2027), not filed owner's earnings. The sweep scores filed OE; on that basis there is nothing to discount.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow, real franchise, unproven cash conversion
- FOR: leading independent position in the CFM56/V2500 aftermarket — the two largest narrowbody engine fleets, with a long run-out tail as fleets age; the MRE module-exchange model is a genuine cost/time advantage over full shop visits (airlines buy green time, not overhauls); proprietary PMA parts capability; SCI creates captive MRE demand — SPV-owned engines are serviced exclusively by FTAI's shops; scale in used-serviceable-material sourcing (e.g., the 27-aircraft WestJet teardown/lease deal feeding CFM56-7B modules).
- AGAINST: gross margin has compressed every year as product sales mix grows — 95.7% (2021) → 64.9% (2022) → 57.1% (2023) → 52.4% (2024) → 46.2% (2025) (fundamentals.json) — the opposite of demonstrated pricing power at the consolidated level; concentration in two aging engine platforms whose fleets shrink from here; OEMs (CFM/GE Aerospace/Safran) and Willis Lease compete for the same aftermarket; roic_proxy is not computable from the filed tags (operating income untagged in EDGAR for FTAI — fundamentals.json returns null), so there is no filed ROIC history showing returns above cost of capital through a cycle — a 7+ moat is not supportable without it; ~10x debt/equity leverage means the equity is a stub claim on the asset pool.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years. Moot for the score — with a negative base there is no DCF to fade — but recorded for pass 2.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-16)
No scenario table: the engine exits at the data gate's F branch — **no positive normalized conservative owner's earnings**, f_subtype **no_cash_generation** (sum of the last 3 fiscal years' OCF − capex is not positive). Tier by numbers: **F**. Implied IRR and IV@15% are null in dcf_numbers.json — not zero, not estimable. Scenario inputs recorded for consistency (moat 5, probs 10/25/30/25/10, default offsets/mults) but they multiply a negative base and produce nothing quotable. Growth sanity check: revenue prints are real and strong (FY2025 +44.5% YoY; Q2 2026 +40.9% YoY) — growth is not the problem; cash conversion is. Any scenario start would be decoration on a negative base, so none is presented.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 9 months ago): resolved by ttm.py — TTM OE through Q2 2026 is −$4.86/share, worse than the FY2025 −$3.47 and the −$2.00 median. Staleness is not hiding a positive base; no --ttm final run was needed because every candidate base is negative.
- **BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT** (>60% revenue jump in last 5 yrs): named — the 2022 corporate break: Fortress Transportation and Infrastructure Investors spun off its infrastructure business and merged into FTAI Aviation Ltd. (Nov 10, 2022), converting from a diversified transport/infrastructure holder (plus an externally managed structure, internalized May 2024) into a pure aviation company; revenue then scaled $335,583,000 (2021) → $708,411,000 (2022) → $1,170,896,000 (2023) on the aviation-only base plus MRE growth. All CAGRs straddling 2022 (rev_cagr_5y 53.1%, rev_cagr_3y 52.4%) mix the old and new companies and are not used for any verdict — the F rests on OE levels, not growth rates.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2025: NI +$501,064,000 vs OCF −$310,745,000): the gap is the business model's asset churn hitting the two statements differently — net income carries gains on engine/aircraft sales (including sales into the SCI vehicles) and equity-method SCI income, while operating cash flow absorbs the cash cost of acquiring the engines/modules that feed the exchange pool and resale (inventory build; inventory stood at $1,544,592,000 at Q2 2026 per the 10-Q). Earnings with no operating cash behind them for a second straight year (FY2024: NI +$8,682,000 vs OCF −$187,956,000) is exactly what the conservative OE definition exists to catch; the OCF-based series is used throughout, so the divergence does not contaminate the base — it IS the base story.

## Red flags / research notes
- **Short-seller accounting controversy (Jan 2025):** Muddy Waters alleged whole-engine sales were booked as recurring MRE revenue in Aerospace Products, inflating the growth narrative; Snowcap amplified. FTAI's Audit Committee review (independent legal/forensic advisors) concluded the claims were unsupported; a securities class action followed. Unresolved in the market's mind and directly on-point for this sweep: if a large share of segment profit is asset-sale gains rather than recurring service margin, the "recurring EBITDA" the price capitalizes is lower quality than presented. The filed cash flows are consistent with the skeptics' narrower point — profits are not converting to operating cash.
- **Leverage:** net debt $3,148,415,000 vs book equity $334,174,000 (FY2025). The equity story depends on asset values (used engines/aircraft) holding.
- **Platform concentration:** CFM56/V2500 fleets are in long decline; FTAI Power (data-center turbines) is the hedge but has no deliveries until later 2026 and execution risk is real despite the $1.465B anchor contract.
- SBC is modest ($21,733,000 FY2025; $25,008,000 TTM) and share count is nearly flat (share_cagr +1.46%/yr, a small dilution headwind already in the blend) — dilution is not the issue here.

## My thoughts / method range
- Method range is one-sided: median base −$2.00/sh, latest FY −$3.47/sh, TTM −$4.86/sh, maintenance definition −$338,457,000 total. Every filed basis is Tier F. There is no defensible OE base within the bounded override authority that turns this positive — a base_override would have to be built from figures this run printed, and all of them are negative.
- The bull case is an Adjusted-EBITDA / asset-value case (SCI fee stream + Power), not an owner's-earnings case. Pass 2's segment work may show Aerospace Products earning real cash margins inside the consolidated OCF drag; that is the one route that could revisit this F. On pass-1 evidence, the price pays today for cash the filings have not yet produced.
- Hurdle-clearing price: not computable — with a negative OE base there is no positive price at which the OE DCF clears 15%; the stock would need a positive, filing-backed OE base first.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: F** (no_cash_generation; no positive conservative owner's earnings on any basis)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high that filed OE is negative on every basis; medium on how harshly the OE definition treats an engine-pool builder mid-growth — noted, and it does not change the tier)
- One-liner: Real CFM56/V2500 aftermarket franchise (moat 5/10) priced like a compounder at $169.29, but conservative owner's earnings are negative on every filed basis — median −$2.00/sh, FY2025 −$3.47/sh, TTM −$4.86/sh — so no OE DCF supports the price and it cannot clear the 15% hurdle.
